hero.body: GPT‑Admin is an MCP hub. Plug your servers and any MCP (chrome‑devtools, openmemory) into it, and your favourite AI connects to the hub in one of three ways. Manage everything from web search to spinning up subagents.

author.body1: Hey, I'm not a corporation. I'm a real person doing this solo — for fun and for myself. I've been using the project for over a year; it's more convenient than Codex or Claude for infrastructure work.
author.body2: It's not a full replacement, it's a complement — a tool for servers and admin work. I have 8B tokens in Codex and 2B in Claude, but for my own machines this is faster. Bugs are possible — write me, I'll fix it.

useCases.body: The capabilities come from the hub itself, not from a specific adapter. Whatever AI you connect — Claude, DeepSeek or ChatGPT — it gets access to all of it.

items.title: Server administration
items.body: Restart systemd, firewall, nginx, fail2ban, sshd. Install software, edit configs, open ports — and verify the result.

items.title: Writing and running code
items.body: Edits code, runs checks, can spawn a subagent — "run codex to fix this bug" while you do something else.

items.title: Fix and clean up PRs
items.body: Finds the fork in memory, keeps a single feature commit, runs type-check/lint/build and force-pushes over SSH.

items.title: Log inspection
items.body: Parses journalctl, nginx, postgres logs, finds anomalies, suggests fixes and applies them after confirmation.

items.title: Web search
items.body: Through the chrome-devtools MCP — the agent itself opens pages, reads docs and searches for a solution, without leaving the chat.

items.title: Incident diagnostics
items.body: Finds the failed service itself, reads logs, understands the cause (ECONNREFUSED, 503, OOM) and fixes it — with a report and checks.

adapters.body: These aren't three separate products, they are three adapters to the same hub. Pick the one that fits your AI — capabilities are the same.

items.title: ChatGPT · Open WebUI
items.body: Custom GPT, Open WebUI or Apps SDK widget right in chat. ChatGPT itself figures out when to run a command. No paid Codex limits.

items.title: Claude · Codex · OpenCode
items.body: GPT‑Admin works as MCP remote SSE. Connect it in your client settings — and the AI gets native tool calls across your entire infrastructure.

items.title: DeepSeek · Qwen · Alice
items.body: A userscript for Tampermonkey / Firefox adds MCP buttons to free web AIs. No paid API needed — just a free web chat.

footer.tagline: Built for those tired of copy-pasting commands

pageChatgpt.lead: Create a Custom GPT with an action: import the OpenAPI of the whole hub or of a single MCP server, plug in the Hub URL and Bearer key — and ChatGPT only calls the tools you allow. No API limits, no paid Codex.

benefits.title: No Codex limits
benefits.body: The Custom GPT runs commands through your hub — no hourly or daily tool-call quotas. No paid Codex required.

benefits.title: Real execution
benefits.body: Not "here's the command, copy-paste it" — ChatGPT itself runs the command, reads logs, validates and reports real output.

benefits.title: Under your control
benefits.body: Commands only flow through your hub and your Bearer key. No own domain needed — auto-tunnel via FRP.

pageChatgpt.step1Body: One command installs the hub-proxy and shellmcp. The installer picks the mode (user/system) automatically. After install, you'll get the Hub URL and CTL_TOKEN (Bearer) — save them.
pageChatgpt.step1CastCaption: Below: a real recording of a full install — old state is removed, then hub, ShellMCP and FRP are set up.
pageChatgpt.step2Body: Go to chatgpt.com/gpts/editor and create a new GPT (or open an existing one).
pageChatgpt.step3Body: In "Configure" → "Actions" → "Create new action". Choose Import by URL and paste the OpenAPI endpoint of the whole hub or a single MCP server:
pageChatgpt.step3Hint: For the whole GPTAdmin, use the common /actions/openapi.yaml. For a single MCP, use /server/{slug}/actions/openapi.yaml — e.g. OpenMemory.
pageChatgpt.step4Body: In "Authentication", pick type API key, scheme Bearer, and paste your CTL_TOKEN.
pageChatgpt.step5Body: "Install nginx", "fix the site", "show memory". ChatGPT itself calls the secure GPTAdmin gateway and gets a response from the chosen MCP server — without exposing the whole relay if you picked a per-server Action.
pageChatgpt.widgetBody: GPT‑Admin exposes an Apps SDK widget — right inside any ChatGPT chat. ChatGPT itself figures out when to read your code, run a command, or check the logs. The widget shows input, result, and background-job polling — in real time, inside the conversation.
pageChatgpt.autoConfirmBody: By default, ChatGPT asks for your approval before every command. Want autopilot? Install auto-confirm-extension — a browser extension that automatically approves tool calls. Fully reversible: turn it off and ChatGPT will start asking again.
pageChatgpt.ctaTitle: Need MCP for Claude or free AIs?
pageChatgpt.ctaBody: GPT‑Admin works two more ways: as an MCP server for Claude/Codex/OpenCode and as a browser extension for free web AIs.

pageMcpServer.lead: GPT‑Admin is an MCP-compatible gateway. Plug in the whole hub or a single per-server URL like /server/{slug}/mcp — and the AI gets native tool calls through a secure relay.
pageMcpServer.sectionBody: The hub proxies commands, shellmcp runs them locally. Any MCP-compatible client gets access to Linux, macOS, and Windows machines — or to a single picked MCP server, e.g. OpenMemory.
sectionPoints: Install any MCP once — available to every agent
Commands run locally; results return to the agent
pageMcpServer.openmemoryQuote: I personally installed openmemory so that different AIs know everything about my projects.
pageMcpServer.step1Body: Install the hub-proxy and shellmcp on your main PC/VPS, and shellmcp alone on every other machine. After install you get the Hub URL and CTL_TOKEN.
pageMcpServer.step2Title: Add the MCP server to your client
pageMcpServer.step2Body: In your client's settings (Claude Desktop → claude_desktop_config.json, Codex, OpenCode) add GPT‑Admin as MCP remote SSE (Streamable HTTP):
pageMcpServer.step2Note: This endpoint goes through the OAuth flow. Don't plug CTL_TOKEN in here as a bearer for /mcp. See the #/docs section for details.
pageMcpServer.codexLocalTitle: Codex on macOS: add a local MCP without reinstalling
pageMcpServer.codexLocalBody: If GPT‑Admin is already installed and the hub is running on http://127.0.0.1:9001/mcp, run the command below. The script pulls a Codex token from the local gptadmin.env, adds bearer_token_env_var, and replaces the old no-auth MCP entry.
pageMcpServer.step3Body: Claude Desktop / Codex / OpenCode picks up the new MCP server on next launch. Verify that commands appear in the tools list.
pageMcpServer.step4Body: "Install WireGuard", "fix nginx". The AI itself calls the right tools, runs commands through the hub, and returns a report.
pageMcpServer.ctaTitle: No paid AI? Try the extension
pageMcpServer.ctaBody: The browser extension turns free web AIs (Qwen, GigaChat, Alice) into a GPT‑Admin client — no API, no subscriptions.

pageMcpExtension.lead: A userscript for Tampermonkey/Firefox adds MCP buttons right into the ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, Alice and Sber interfaces. No paid API needed — just a free web chat.
pageMcpExtension.platformsBody: A userscript works anywhere there's a script manager.
pageMcpExtension.step1Body: Tampermonkey (Chrome), Userscripts (iPhone Safari), or Firefox + Tampermonkey (Android).
pageMcpExtension.step2Body: Click the install button — the manager picks up the .user.js and offers to install it.
pageMcpExtension.step3Body: Press Alt+K and paste the key from your hub.
pageMcpExtension.step4Title: Open any chat and press MCP All
pageMcpExtension.step4Body: Alt+M inserts the prompt into the input box. The AI runs commands through your hub.
pageMcpExtension.ctaBody: For Claude, Codex and OpenCode there's the MCP server; for ChatGPT there's the no-limits Custom GPT.

stepsHow.title: MCP All
stepsHow.body: Inserts a compact description of every MCP agent and its tools into the chat input. The prompt is also copied to clipboard — Alt+M.

stepsHow.title: MCP — pick one
stepsHow.body: Opens a panel to pick a specific agent with detailed descriptions of each tool.

stepsHow.title: Auto-run
stepsHow.body: If the AI replies with a ```mcp-fenced JSON block — the script POSTs it to the hub and pastes the result back into the chat.

platforms.title: macOS · Windows · Linux

platforms.title: iPhone

platforms.title: Android
